subtype: Bowing the head in respect and mourning [Expressing]
passage: Note, Saturday. I am Chetan, a colleague of Leela's from the district office. At her grandfather's funeral, Leela stood at the back of the family group with her head bowed for most of the ceremony, hands folded. She did not speak to anyone until the end. When the priest lit the lamp she bowed lower. Others in the family did the same, some with a namaste, some touching the ground. I followed the family's lead and bowed my head and stayed quiet. Afterwards Leela thanked me for coming and her eyes were red. I did not ask questions. I offered to bring lunch to the house on Monday and she agreed.

qa.q: Where did Leela stand during the funeral?
qa.a: She stood at the back of the family group with her head bowed.

qa.q: What did Leela's bowed head most likely mean, and what else could it mean?
qa.a: It most likely showed respect and grief for her grandfather, and her red eyes fit that. It could also be a custom of the family or prayer, since meanings shift with tradition.

qa.q: How did Chetan behave with care at the funeral?
qa.a: Chetan followed the family's lead, stayed quiet, did not ask questions and offered practical help with lunch on Monday.

qa.q: How might Leela's family see a colleague who followed their customs at the funeral?
qa.a: They would probably see it as respectful and caring, since the colleague did not impose a personal way of behaving.

grounding: Colleague's note about an adult bowing the head at a funeral to show respect and grief, with observers following local custom.

subtype: Bowing the head in respect and mourning [Expressing]
passage: Thursday, late. Went to Nadeem uncle's funeral prayers today with Papa. When the body was brought in, I bowed my head along with everyone and kept my eyes down. I am Kamal. I felt a heavy quiet in my chest. Nadeem uncle used to hand me sweets when I was small. Beside me Rukmini, from my old building, had her head down and her lips moving without sound. I wondered if she was praying or just holding herself together. At the gate an old man greeted Papa with a bow of the head and a hand on his chest, and Papa did the same. Different from what we do at temple, but I understood it. I stayed a while at home in silence.

qa.q: Who accompanied Kamal to the funeral prayers?
What did Kamal feel at the funeral, and what did he wonder about Rukmini?
qa.a: He felt a heavy quiet and sadness, remembering the uncle who gave him sweets. He wondered whether Rukmini was praying or holding herself together, which shows he did not assume.

qa.q: What did Kamal do that fitted the setting?
qa.a: He bowed his head and kept his eyes down like the others and understood the different greeting at the gate, following local custom.

qa.q: How might the old man at the gate have seen Papa's return greeting?
qa.a: He probably took it as a shared gesture of respect and condolence, though Papa's temple custom is different.

grounding: Diary entry of an adult bowing the head at a funeral, where meaning depends on setting and tradition and observers follow custom.
